feedback: If the Atlantic and Pacific are swapped, or the Indian is misplaced, show the correct basin and have the learner re-place it, naming a neighbouring continent as a landmark.
If the Southern or Arctic is omitted, point to Antarctica (Southern rings it) and the icy top of the globe (Arctic) and add the missing labels.
Confirm success when the learner places at least three correctly, then challenge them to complete all five from memory.
activities.intendedInsight: Reliable location memory comes from repeated active placement and self-correction, anchored by a memorable fact for each ocean.
learnerActions: On a blank or unlabelled world map, place or write each of the five ocean names in the correct basin: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic.
Repeat the placement several times across the session (not once) until you can place at least three reliably, then all five.
Attach a memory hook to each: Pacific = biggest, Arctic = smallest and partly covered by floating sea ice at the top, Southern = rings Antarctica at the bottom, plus Atlantic and Indian between them.
Check your placement against a labelled reference map and correct any swaps.
activities.title: Name and place the five oceans

feedback: If the learner says the fish would be blocked by land, return to the globe trace and show the continuous route, naming the boundaries as human lines on connected water.
If they say the colours or names mean different water, show that the same salty water flows across the drawn line.
Affirm a full answer that names a continuous route round the continents and distinguishes the human-made names from the physical water.
activities.intendedInsight: A learner who holds the connected-ocean concept can justify that water (and a fish) can travel between any oceans, because the basins join around the continents; naming is for human convenience.
learnerActions: Answer the travel question: if a drop of dye (or a fish) started in the middle of the Pacific, could it ever reach the Atlantic without leaving the water? Explain how.
Decide true or false: 'the oceans are separate seas walled off from each other by land', and justify your choice.
Identify which ocean is largest and which is coldest, and find the coldest one on a globe (at the very top, around the North Pole, where much of the water is covered by floating sea ice).
Explain why people gave one connected ocean five different names.
activities.title: Would the dye reach the other ocean? (reasoning check)
